detailed_rationale:
Sonata Software's Q4 FY26 results tell a margin-led, not topline-led, growth story: consolidated PAT grew 25% QoQ and 21.4% YoY, but revenue was essentially flat-to-down YoY (Rs 25.36bn vs Rs 26.2bn), with the improvement coming entirely from EBITDA margin expansion to 8.23% from 6.60% a year earlier. The company won 8 large deals across FY26 (including two in Q4 with a global fintech/payments company and a PE-backed software holding company), recorded $16.9mn in AI-led project wins in the quarter with an AI-led pipeline of $280mn, and has meaningfully shifted its mix toward Cloud & Data, now 65% of revenue versus 52% in FY24 - a real structural repositioning toward higher-value, presumably higher-margin work.

A leadership transition is underway (a CEO-designate has been named), which is a governance item worth tracking but reads as a planned succession rather than an abrupt departure-under-a-cloud - not, on the evidence available, a red flag in itself. The 1-year revenue growth of just 5.4% (well below the 3-year CAGR of 12.8%) reflects the broader softness in global IT discretionary/enterprise spending that has affected the sector generally, not something specific to Sonata's execution.

Reverse-DCF read: at 18.6x earnings, the market is pricing a modest, margin-recovery-led growth path consistent with the current environment - not aggressive topline assumptions. Given ROE of 26.5% and ROCE of 31.2%, the business remains capital-efficient even in a soft-topline environment, but the case for a re-rating depends on discretionary IT spending recovering, which is a macro call outside the company's control.
recommendation_rationale: Quant model calls Hold (61.0/60.0) reflecting the tension between strong capital efficiency (ROE/ROCE in the high-20s/low-30s%) and weak recent topline growth (5.4% 1yr). Nothing in the fresh research shifts this either direction - margin-led earnings growth in a soft-topline environment is a real but modest positive, not enough to rescue toward a stronger call, and the CEO transition is a watch item, not an escalation-worthy governance concern on current evidence.
summary: Sonata Software's recent profit growth (up over 20% year-on-year) is coming from margin improvement and mix-shift toward higher-value cloud, data and AI work, not from revenue growth, which has been close to flat in a soft global IT-spending environment. The company continues to win large multi-year deals and is building a meaningful AI-related pipeline, and a planned CEO transition is underway. We see this as a capital-efficient business navigating a genuinely weak topline environment reasonably well, priced fairly for that reality rather than for a sharp recovery.
positive_para: Strong capital efficiency (ROE 26.5%, ROCE 31.2%) even in a soft-topline year; real mix-shift toward Cloud & Data (65% of revenue, up from 52% in FY24) and a genuine AI-led deal pipeline ($280mn); continued large-deal wins (8 in FY26) show the sales engine is working even as overall IT discretionary spend stays weak.
negative_para: Revenue growth has stalled to just 5.4% YoY (in fact essentially flat to down in the most recent quarter), meaning recent profit growth is entirely margin-led and has a natural ceiling without a topline recovery; a CEO transition adds near-term leadership-continuity uncertainty even if framed as planned succession; the business remains exposed to global enterprise IT-spending cycles largely outside its control.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At 18.6x earnings, the market is pricing modest, margin-recovery-led growth consistent with the current soft IT-spending backdrop - a fair, not demanding, multiple given ROE/ROCE in the high-20s/low-30s%. Re-rating would require a genuine topline recovery, which depends on a macro (global enterprise IT spend) recovery rather than anything purely company-specific.
